necessary_context.content: The paper uses an n-dimensional space E with B=B* positive definite, primal norm ||x||=<Bx,x>^{1/2}, dual norm ||s||_*=<s,B^{-1}s>^{1/2}, and Gaussian covariance B^{-1}. The selected Algorithm and Theorem records explicitly specialize to E=R^n and B=I; they do not assert a new coordinate-transfer result.
necessary_context.name: Geometry and selected specialization

necessary_context.content: C^{0,0}(E) means |f(x)-f(y)|<=L0(f)||x-y|| for all x,y in E. Section 4 assumes convex f, closed convex Q subset E, and an attained minimum f*=f(x*) with x* in Q. Gaussian trial points can lie outside Q, so f and its value Oracle are required on E.
necessary_context.name: Global model and constrained minimum

necessary_context.applies_to: Selected mu>0 Algorithm and its Proof
necessary_context.content: For mu>0, f_mu(x)=E_u f(x+mu u). Equation (21) identifies its gradient with the expectation of g_mu(x,u)=[f(x+mu u)-f(x)]Bu/mu. With B=I this is the estimator in the selected records. The directional-derivative estimator g_0 is a different Oracle and is excluded.
necessary_context.name: Smoothing and finite-value estimator

necessary_context.content: U_k=(u_0,...,u_k) consists of iid directions; phi_0=f(x0), phi_k=E_{U_{k-1}}f(x_k) for k>=1. S_N=sum_{k=0}^N h_k. The output hat{x}_N minimizes the actual function values over x0,...,xN, not over Gaussian trial points.
